summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971). He held posts at Doshisha University (~1972–1990) and served as professor at Kyoto University (~1990–2007).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indologist attested in 1987 as head (会長) of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai, where he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama.
Tsutomu Horio is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1990.
Tsutomu Kubo was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1908). He later held an academic post at Tohoku University (~1926–1944).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

Tu Weiming is a philosopher and Sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard. He taught at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard—serving as Harvard-Yenching Institute Director (~1996–2008)—and Peking University (~2010).
Tukaram Krishna Laddu was an Indologist and linguist who completed studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912. He held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.

Tulku Sherdor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, under teachers including Ted Norton, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.
Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo and Khenpo Chemchok. He later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist master who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught numerous students, including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Turrell V. Wylie was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci (~1956–1958). He spent his career at the University of Washington, becoming associate professor in 1959 and professor in 1970.

Tyler Dewar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Nitartha Institute. His traditional teachers include Acharya Tashi Wangchuk (2003–2004) and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (attested 2019).

Tzungkuen Wen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Queensland (-2009) under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He served as a lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.
Tōru Funayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner, later holding posts at Kyushu University and Kyoto University.

U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2017), supervised by Sanu Mahatthanadull with committee member Walmoruwe Piyaratana.
Ugyen Pelgen specializes in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held an academic post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh studied at the University of Copenhagen and Karmapa International Buddhist Institute. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he held appointments at Copenhagen, Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, Sydney, and ANU.

Ulrike Roesler earned her PhD at the University of Münster. A specialist in Tibetology and Indology, she taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg before serving as Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford.

Uma Chakravarti is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied at Miranda House (~1958–1962) and the University of Delhi (~1962–1981), where she completed doctoral research under D. Devahuti.
